collected_dynamic_variables.pain_points: Missing calls / calls going unanswered; about 9 missed calls per week, Callers go to the next plumber when calls are missed, Roughly half of missed calls would have booked, Call-backs aren’t always fast/consistent because owner is busy
collected_dynamic_variables.pain_frame: About 9 missed calls a week. Unbelievable.

transcript:
User: Yeah, what.
Agent: Yeah, I am—I’m Linda, an AI assistant on Jay’s team at Dialux, and I help get the walkthroughs set up. What made you call today?
User: Didn't call. You called me. What's this about?
Agent: Got it—sorry about the confusion. We reach out to local businesses because a missed call can mean a missed job, and Dialux helps make sure those calls get handled when your team’s busy. What kind of business are you running?
User: Plumbing. Szymanski & Sons. Missed calls? How many?
Agent: Got it—plumbing, Szymanski & Sons. I don’t have your exact missed-call count in front of me; about how many calls do you think you miss on a typical day (including after-hours)?
User: About 9 missed calls a week. Unbelievable.
Agent: Yeah… 9 missed calls a week is a lot. When those calls go unanswered, what usually happens—do they leave a voicemail, text, or just call the next plumber?
User: Usually call next plumber. Maybe half would've booked. Sure, sure.
Agent: Makes sense—if they call the next plumber, that’s revenue walking out the door. When you do miss a call, who (if anyone) is supposed to call them back, and how fast does that usually happen?
User: I call back. When I can. Not always fast. Spare me.
Agent: Totally hear you—you’re on jobs, so call-backs slip. If those ~9 missed calls a week got answered live and half booked, would you want that handled for you automatically?
User: Sure, sure. Automatically handled? Maybe. How much? What’s the catch?
Agent: Fair question—no “gotcha,” it’s just a monthly service and it depends on your call volume and what you want it to handle, so Jay covers exact pricing on the walkthrough. Before we even go there, mind if I do a 30‑second back-of-napkin math with your numbers so you can tell if it’s even worth it?
User: Fine, but be quick about it. What's the math?
Agent: Got it—I’ll be quick. What’s your average job value, roughly (like $400, $650, $850)?
User: Average job's around $380. What's next?
Agent: So… 9 missed calls/week × ~50% booking × $380 is about **$1,710/week**, or roughly **$7,400/month** leaking when you can’t pick up. It’s a 20-minute walkthrough—what’s better for you, later today or tomorrow?
User: Fine, fine. Book the thing. Tomorrow. What's the time?
Agent: Got it—tomorrow works. And which time zone are you in: Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: Central time. What time tomorrow?
Agent: Perfect—Central time. Before I can lock in times, what’s your first name?
User: Gene. Szymanski & Sons. Just book it. Spare me.
Agent: Got it, Gene. Is the number you’re calling from—**(816) 555-0022**—the best number to reach you?
User: Yeah, that's the number. Now hurry up.
Agent: Alright—tomorrow I can get you in as soon as **10:00 AM** or **10:45 AM** Central time. Which works?
User: Fine, 10:00 AM. Just do it. Done now?
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Hang with me one second—I'm re-confirming it on my side.
Agent: We’re having trouble confirming the calendar right now—I’ve got you penciled for **tomorrow (Wed, Aug 26) at 10:00 AM Central**, and we’ll reach you at **+1 (816) 555-0022** within the hour to lock it in. Anything else you want Jay to cover on that walkthrough?
User: Sure, sure. Fine. Just hurry up, will ya? Unbelievable.
Agent: Got it, Gene—we’ll get this locked in for tomorrow at 10:00 AM Central and you’ll get the confirmation as soon as the calendar cooperates. Thanks for your time, and have a good rest of your day.
